name: TLV493D 3D magnetic sensor
description: Infineon 3-axis Hall-effect magnetic sensor: Bx, By and Bz up to ±130 mT with 12-bit resolution (0.098 mT/LSB) plus an on-chip temperature sensor, over I2C. The chip runs on 2.8–3.5 V; the breakout adds a 3.3 V regulator and level shifters so it works from 3.3 V or 5 V. Too insensitive for a compass: it tracks nearby magnets (joysticks, knobs, lid sensors). Sold as: Adafruit TLV493D Triple-Axis Magnetometer - STEMMA QT / Qwiic (product 4366; 5-pin header VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA), I2C address 0x5E.
eli5: Feels where a nearby magnet is in three directions, so you can make magnetic joysticks, knobs and lid sensors.

supplierQuery: Adafruit TLV493D triple-axis magnetometer STEMMA QT 4366
buildNotes: The chip powers up in power-down mode and measures nothing until configured: read all 10 read registers, copy the factory bits (read reg 7 bits 4:3, reg 8, reg 9 bits 4:0) into write registers 1–3, set the mode and the odd-parity bit, then write all 4 write registers as a raw byte stream (no register address).
Reads always start at register 0: read 7 bytes. Bx = reg0<<4 | reg4>>4, By = reg1<<4 | reg4 & 0x0F, Bz = reg2<<4 | reg5 & 0x0F, 12-bit two's complement, 0.098 mT/LSB.
There are no shadow registers: discard a frame whose channel bits (reg3 bits 1:0) are not 0.
The address is latched from the SDA level at power-up/reset: 0x5E with SDA high (normal on this board), 0x1F with SDA low.
Power VIN from 3.3 V or 5 V; never feed 3Vo, it is the regulator's output.
It cannot see the Earth's field usefully; test it with a small neodymium magnet a few cm away (strong magnets up close saturate at ±130 mT).

driver.code:
# TLV493D-A1B6 3D magnetic sensor (Infineon), MicroPython driver.
# The chip has no register pointer: every read starts at read register 0 and every write is a raw
# byte stream into write registers 0..3. Start-up follows the Infineon user manual / reference library:
# power up (starts in power-down mode), read all 10 read registers, copy the factory bits into the
# write registers, choose a mode, set the odd-parity bit and write all 4 write registers.
import time

ADDR_HIGH = 0x5E  # ADDR/SDA high at power-up (Adafruit breakout default)
ADDR_LOW = 0x1F   # ADDR/SDA low at power-up

MT_PER_LSB = 0.098   # 12-bit two's complement, 0.098 mT/LSB (datasheet table 10)
T25_LSB = 340        # temperature raw value at 25 degC (datasheet table 8)
DEG_PER_LSB = 1.1    # degC per LSB


def _s12(v):
    return v - 4096 if v & 0x800 else v


class TLV493D:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=ADDR_HIGH, reset=True):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if reset:
            # I2C reset: general-call address 0x00; the data byte sets the SDA level the chip samples
            # for its address (0xFF -> 0x5E, 0x00 -> 0x1F), as in Infineon's library.
            try:
                i2c.writeto(0x00, b'\xff' if addr == ADDR_HIGH else b'\x00')
            except OSError:
                pass  # the chip need not acknowledge the reset frame
        time.sleep_ms(40)
        r = i2c.readfrom(addr, 10)
        w = bytearray(4)
        w[0] = 0x00                 # reserved
        w[1] = r[7] & 0x18          # MOD1: factory bits 4:3, IICAddr 00 (keep address), INT off
        w[2] = r[8]                 # reserved factory byte
        w[3] = r[9] & 0x1F          # MOD2: factory bits 4:0
        w[1] |= 0x01                # LOW = 1, FAST = 0 -> low-power mode
        w[3] |= 0x40 | 0x20         # LP period 12 ms (~100 Hz), parity test enabled, temperature on (bit 7 = 0)
        w[1] |= 0x80                # parity bit: all bits of the 4 bytes must have odd parity
        y = w[0] ^ w[1] ^ w[2] ^ w[3]
        y ^= y >> 4
        y ^= y >> 2
        y ^= y >> 1
        if not (y & 1):
            w[1] &= 0x7F
        i2c.writeto(addr, w)
        time.sleep_ms(15)           # first conversion

    def read_raw(self):
        # No shadow registers: only accept a frame whose channel bits are 0 (conversion finished).
        for _ in range(5):
            d = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 7)
            if d[3] & 0x03 == 0:
                break
            time.sleep_ms(2)
        else:
            raise OSError('TLV493D: conversion never finished')
        bx = _s12((d[0] << 4) | (d[4] >> 4))
        by = _s12((d[1] << 4) | (d[4] & 0x0F))
        bz = _s12((d[2] << 4) | (d[5] & 0x0F))
        t = _s12(((d[3] & 0xF0) << 4) | d[6])
        return bx, by, bz, t

    def read(self):
        """Return (Bx, By, Bz) in mT and the chip temperature in degC."""
        bx, by, bz, t = self.read_raw()
        return (bx * MT_PER_LSB, by * MT_PER_LSB, bz * MT_PER_LSB,
                (t - T25_LSB) * DEG_PER_LSB + 25)

    def magnetic(self):
        return self.read()[:3]

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[3]

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from tlv493d import TLV493D

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = TLV493D(i2c)
while True:
    bx, by, bz, t = sensor.read()
    print('X=%.1f Y=%.1f Z=%.1f T=%.1f' % (bx, by, bz, t))
    time.sleep(1)
